note.text: A long, thin, slippery body lets an earthworm push through soil, digging tunnels as it goes.

steps.title: Segments
steps.instruction: Draw the rings that divide the body into segments.

note.text: The body is made of many ring-shaped segments. Each has tiny bristles, called setae, that grip the soil as the worm moves.

steps.title: Clitellum
steps.instruction: Trace the wide band near the front end.

note.text: This thick band is the clitellum. It makes a cocoon where the worm's eggs are kept, so it helps earthworms reproduce.

steps.title: Mouth
steps.instruction: Dab the mouth at the front end.

note.text: Earthworms eat soil as they burrow, digesting the tiny bits of dead plants and living things in it.

steps.title: Label the parts
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered part.

targets.role: One of many rings, each with gripping bristles.

commonMistakes.Tail: The tail end is at the far right. This part is near the front.

steps.title: Explain
steps.instruction: Think about how an earthworm breathes.
steps.question: Earthworms have no lungs. Why do they need to stay damp?

options.text: They breathe through their skin, which only works when it's moist
options.feedback: Yes. Oxygen passes in through their moist skin. If an earthworm dries out, it can't breathe.
Earthworms don't swim. Damp skin lets them take in oxygen.
They eat bits of dead plants in soil. Moist skin is for breathing.
The bristles grip the soil. Moist skin is what lets them breathe.
